# Forks — content is TOML-only

## F1 — the art manifests live with the tree they index {#f1}

_2026-08-04._ `content/visual/manifest/*.rd` is a generated existence index of the texture master
tree: per kind leaf, its variant ids, layer count, part ids, subkind overrides, content hash and
which maps exist. It is derived data about `textures/`, and `textures/` is gitignored ("derived/
regenerated by `bin/art`, served from R2").

**Chosen**: `textures/manifest/<type>.json` — untracked, regenerated by `bin/art manifest`,
uploaded alongside the masters by the same publish tail that produces them ([bin/art:2700](../../../bin/art)
already couples `cmd_manifest` to `cmd_upload_master`). An index and its subject share a lifetime;
a checkout without masters must not carry an index of textures it does not have.

Rejected: **tracking it at a new root** (`art/manifest/`) — a tracked index of an untracked tree
is stale on every clone and no gate can catch it. **Leaving it in `content/` as TOML** — it is not
authored and not the game's; that fails the one rule this stream exists to state. **Deleting it
outright** — the four fields `tex_manifest` does not carry ([F5](#f5)) would be lost, and
`preserve-future-intent` says build toward the documented `^r2` resolver, not around it.

## F2 — a machine index is JSON {#f2}

_2026-08-04._ Once the manifest leaves `content/`, its format is free. The file is written by a
bash generator and read by the client's resolver; no human edits it, and the header has said
`Do not edit by hand` since it was ported.

**Chosen**: JSON. It is what the client already consumes for the sibling index
(`/textures-manifest`, [tex_manifest.rs](../../../server/edge/src/tex_manifest.rs)), it needs no
parser on either side, and it converges with [F5](#f5) where the two indexes become one.

Rejected: **TOML** — TOML's virtue is diffable hand-authoring, which this file explicitly forbids;
adopting it here would make "TOML" mean "a file format we like" instead of "the authored corpus",
and the rule in [P4](todo.md) would lose its meaning. **Keeping the `.rd` spelling** — the dialect
has no parser left in the repo; a syntax with no reader is a fossil, and `delete-don't-deprecate`
applies to formats too.

## F3 — deployment topology moves out with its format intact {#f3}

_2026-08-04._ `content/servers/<env>` is a whitespace-column file (`server` / `shard` / `region` /
`cold` rows) read by `bin/lib/index.sh` through `rd_servers_manifest`
([bin/lib/common.sh:121](../../../bin/lib/common.sh)). Clients never read it; the game never reads
it. It is `rd redeploy`'s input that happens to live in `content/`.

**Chosen**: move to `deploy/servers/<env>`, format unchanged. The move is what the rule requires;
the format is fine where it is read from.

Rejected: **converting it to TOML** — the only reader is bash, and parsing TOML in bash means
either hand-rolling a parser or shelling to python for a six-row file. That is real complexity
bought to satisfy a rule about the *corpus*, which this file is not part of. **Leaving it in
`content/`** — it would be the permanent exception that makes the gate advisory, and an exception
a gate has to special-case is how the next four files get in.

## F4 — the R2 corpus index is deleted, not refreshed {#f4}

_2026-08-04._ `content/manifest.json` exists because the edge's R2 source "can't list a bucket"
([content.rs:118](../../../server/edge/src/content.rs)). It lists five `.rd` keys that were
deleted on 2026-08-04, so `load_r2` fetches the first key and fails — the deployed content path is
broken today ([I2](issues.md#i2)).

**Chosen**: delete the file and `bin/dsl reindex`; the edge lists `<prefix>/content/` via SigV4
`ListObjectsV2` (R2 is S3-compatible and `rusty_s3` already signs the actions the edge uses) and
takes every `*.toml` key, sorted. The bucket becomes self-describing and a stale index stops being
a thing that can exist.

Rejected: **regenerating `manifest.json` over the TOMLs** — it is a second place recording which
files exist, it went stale within one stream of being written, and nothing verifies it. **Hard-
coding the five basenames in the edge** — the same second place, now in Rust and needing a
redeploy to add a file.

Known limit, accepted: this repo has no R2 credentials (`bin/keys` is empty), so the listing path
cannot be exercised live here. Acceptance is a unit test over the key filter plus a clean build;
recorded as [I3](issues.md#i3) so the first real deploy knows to watch it.

## F6 — the `"rd"` wire key is renamed, in P4, as its own coordinated change {#f6}

_2026-08-04, found while executing P1._ The `/content` payload is
`{ "version": "<hex>", "rd": [[name, text], …] }` and three consumers destructure that `rd` key:
the webgl client's `contentBoot.ts:72`, the npc's `lib.rs:224`, and the edge's own snapshot test.
The dialect it is named after has been deleted; the key is now a fossil in a live protocol.

**Chosen**: rename it to `"toml"` in P4's truth pass, edge and all three consumers in **one**
commit, with the redeploy + a client boot as acceptance. Not in P1: P1's claim is "the deleted
things are deleted", and a wire rename spanning three consumers has a different blast radius and
deserves its own verification. Alongside it go the stale `.rd` prose comments now scattered
through `client/webgl` (`WorldBridge`, `Viewport`, `worldTilt`, `material`, `contentBoot`),
`shared/wasm/src/lib.rs`, `client/npc/src/lib.rs`, and `server/edge/src/{config,worldgen}.rs` —
they cite `content/visual/things.rd` and friends as if those files existed.

Rejected: **renaming it inside P1** (a protocol change smuggled into a deletion commit — if the
client black-screens, the bisect points at five unrelated things; the previous stream's embed
incident is exactly this failure). **Leaving `"rd"` forever** (`delete-don't-deprecate`: an
authoritative name may not lie, and a wire field is as authoritative as names get). **A
compatibility window accepting both keys** — there is one server and one client, deployed
together; a dual-read path would outlive its reason.

## F7 — `bin/dsl` renames to `bin/content`, in P4 {#f7}

_2026-08-04, found while executing P2._ The tool now publishes a flat TOML corpus and has no
folder concept, no index, and no connection to the dialect it is named after. `docs-authority`
says an authoritative name may not lie, and a CLI's name is as authoritative as it gets.

**Chosen**: rename in P4's truth pass, alongside `bin/art`'s reference, `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`'s
`dev/` component list, and the `dsl-script-ported` memory — one commit, so the name and everything
that cites it move together. A pointer sits in the script's own header until then, so anyone
reading it learns the name is a fossil.

Rejected: **renaming inside P2** (P2's claim is about where the manifests live; a rename of a
different tool touches docs and memories and would blur that). **Keeping `dsl`** — the previous
stream already deleted a crate for exactly this reason ([toml-content F4](../2026-08-04-toml-content/forks.md#f4)),
and leaving the CLI named after the deleted thing re-opens the question every time someone reads
`bin/`.

## F8 — the texture-index merge waits for R2 mode to be real {#f8}

_2026-08-04, supersedes [F5](#f5)'s plan (not its goal), on the evidence in
[I9](issues.md#i9)._ The merge as planned would port four fields that are already served (variants
and parts as stem keys, `layers` as the part count) or empty everywhere (`subkinds`). Building it
would add schema nothing reads.

The reason the generator can't just be deleted instead is the opposite of what F5 assumed:
`tex_manifest` is **disk-only**, and in R2 mode the edge serves an empty manifest. The offline
generator is the documented answer for that mode.

**Chosen: stop here, structurally.** `bin/art manifest` keeps producing
`textures/manifest/<type>.json` — right home, right format, [P2](todo.md) settled that — and
`/textures-manifest` stays the live index. The two do not conflict today because only one runs in
any given mode. The merge is recorded in
[`components/server/edge/intent/texture-index.md`](../../components/server/edge/intent/texture-index.md)
and executes when R2 mode is real enough to test.

Rejected, and why each is worse than waiting:

- **Make `bin/art` emit the edge's exact schema.** The rows differ where it is expensive: the edge
  hashes **per stem** (16 hex, from the leaf's own bytes), `bin/art` hashes **per kind** (52-bit
  decimal over the kind's PNGs — the same recipe `art gc` compares against, so it cannot simply
  change). Reimplementing per-stem hashing and image-dimension reading in bash, unverifiable
  against a bucket this repo has no credentials for, buys a schema match nothing consumes yet.
- **Delete `bin/art manifest` outright.** Removes the only planned index for R2 mode to satisfy a
  tidiness rule. `preserve-future-intent` cuts the other way here.
- **Have the edge generate the R2 index too** (scan masters pre-upload, or list the bucket). This
  is probably the right end state — it keeps ONE scanner and ONE hash recipe — but it is a design
  call about a mode that has never run, and deciding it now would be speculative architecture with
  no way to verify it. It belongs in the stream that makes R2 mode real.

## F5 — one texture index is the destination {#f5}

_2026-08-04._ Two indexes scan the same master tree. The edge's `tex_manifest` carries hash,
`maxSize`, lods, maps, grid, pad, span and square, and the client consumes it. The art manifest
carries hash and maps *plus* variant ids, layer count, part ids and subkinds — the existence data
the `^r2` resolver needs so it never speculatively requests a variant that isn't there.

**Chosen**: the merge is the destination, and it is [P5](todo.md) — the last phase, after the move
is complete and gated. Folding the four missing fields into `tex_manifest` makes
`/textures-manifest` the one index and retires `bin/art manifest`'s file output entirely. Doing it
*before* the move would mean rewriting a live client surface inside a diff whose whole claim is
"nothing changed except where the file lives".

Rejected: **merging first** (the above), **never merging** (two indexes of one tree is a second
place to record one fact, which the conventions ban outright).

Conditional, stated: the merge assumes the **edge serves textures**. If R2-direct serving returns,
a client with no edge still needs a fetchable index — which is exactly what [F1](#f1)'s
`textures/manifest/` home, uploaded with the masters, already provides. The merge may then become
"the edge serves the generated file" rather than "the edge generates it". Either way the file has
one home and one format after this stream.
